explain.title: What similar figures mean
explain.body: Your textbook defines similar figures as having the same shape but not necessarily the same size. Two polygons are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and the corresponding sides are proportional (i.e., the ratios of the lengths of corresponding sides are equal). The symbol for similarity is '~'.

explain.title: How to compare sides
explain.body: Match sides that connect corresponding vertices, then write their ratios in the same order. If the ratios are equal, the corresponding sides are proportional. For instance, 6/10.5 = 9/15.75 = 12/21 = 4/7.

explain.title: Ways to identify similar triangles
explain.body: The textbook shows that triangles are similar when two pairs of corresponding angles are equal, when the ratio of two corresponding sides and their included angle are equal, or when all ratios of corresponding sides are equal.

explain.title: Using similarity to find a length
explain.body: Once you know the triangles are similar, write a proportion using corresponding sides. Keep each pair in the same order, substitute the known lengths, and solve for the unknown.

Saying polygons are similar because their angles match without checking that their corresponding sides are proportional.

Leaving off units from a length answer or rounding too early.

explain.title: Similar solids
explain.body: Two solids are said to be similar if they have same shape but possibly different sizes. Their corresponding lengths are proportional.

explain.title: Volume ratio
explain.body: Hence the ratio of the volume of any two similar solids is equal to the cube of the ratio of any two corresponding lengths of the solids. In symbols, V₁/V₂ = (ℓ₁/ℓ₂)³.

explain.title: Scale factor
explain.body: Since each length is k times of the other, we take ℓ₁/ℓ₂ = k, then V₁/V₂ = k³. i.e., Volume V₁ is k³ times the volume V₂ and k is called scale factor.

explain.title: Mass and area ratios
explain.body: Since mass of a substance is proportional to its volume, the ratio of the mass of two similar solids is equal of to the ratio of their volumes. Use w₁/w₂ = (ℓ₁/ℓ₂)³ for masses. For surface areas, square the corresponding length ratio.

mistakes: Using the length ratio directly as the volume ratio instead of cubing it.
Squaring the length ratio when a volume is asked for; squaring is for areas.
Reversing the order of a ratio, for example using smaller/larger lengths with larger/smaller volumes.
Forgetting to take the cube root when volumes are given and the length ratio is required.
Leaving off units in a final volume, area or mass answer.

explain.title: Regular polygons and their angles
explain.body: A regular polygon has all sides and all angles equal. For a polygon with n sides, the sum of its interior angles is (n − 2) × 180°. In a regular polygon, divide this sum by n to get each interior angle. The exterior angles of any polygon add to 360°, so each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 360°/n. At each vertex, an interior angle and its exterior angle add to 180°.

explain.title: Diagonals and symmetry
explain.body: The total number of diagonals in a regular polygon with n sides is n(n − 3)/2. A regular n-sided polygon has rotational symmetry and reflexive symmetry both of order n. It has n lines of symmetry, and a rotation of 360°/n makes it look the same.

explain.title: Triangle properties
explain.body: A triangle's interior angles add to 180°. In an equilateral triangle, all sides are equal and each angle is 60°. In an isosceles triangle, two sides and the angles opposite those equal sides are equal. An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

explain.title: Parallelograms and related shapes
explain.body: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral whose opposite sides are parallel and equal in length and opposite angles are equal. Its adjacent angles are supplementary, and its diagonals bisect each other. A rectangle has all angles 90° and equal diagonals. A rhombus has all sides equal and diagonals that bisect each other at right angles. A square has all sides equal, all angles 90°, and diagonals that are equal and bisect each other at right angles.

explain.title: Tessellations and applications
explain.body: A tessellation is a pattern of shapes that fit together perfectly, without any gaps or overlaps, covering a plane. Equilateral triangles, squares and regular hexagons can tessellate on their own because their angles fit around a point to make 360°. Polygon area and angle properties also help solve problems about floors, walls, windows and other designs.

mistakes: Do not use (n − 2) × 180° as the measure of each interior angle; it gives the sum. Divide by n for each angle of a regular polygon.
Do not confuse an interior angle with an exterior angle: each regular exterior angle is 360°/n.
Do not assume the sloping side of a parallelogram is its height; the height must be perpendicular to the base.
Remember that adjacent angles in a parallelogram add to 180°, while opposite angles are equal.
For area and coverage questions, use square units for area and round a required number of tiles, gallons or litres up when a fraction remains.
Do not claim that regular pentagons tessellate on their own; the angles meeting at a point must add to 360°.

explain.title: What similarity tells you
explain.body: Similar polygons have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. Their shapes match, even if their sizes differ.

explain.title: Areas use the square
explain.body: If corresponding lengths are in the ratio a:b, the areas are in the ratio a²:b². This rule works for similar polygons and for surface areas of similar solids.

explain.title: Volumes and capacities use the cube
explain.body: For similar solids, cube the corresponding-length ratio to find the volume or capacity ratio. For example, a length ratio of 2:1 gives a capacity ratio of 8:1.

explain.title: Regular polygon angles
explain.body: A regular polygon's exterior angles add to 360°. So its number of sides is 360° divided by one exterior angle. An interior angle and its exterior angle add to 180°.

explain.title: Counting diagonals

notes.title: How to identify similar polygons
notes.answer: Two polygons are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are proportional.
notes.explanation: Similar polygons have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. For example, 6/10.5 = 9/15.75 = 12/21 = 4/7, so these corresponding sides are proportional. In a parallelogram, equal angles alone are not enough: the corresponding lengths must also have the same ratio.
notes.simple: Similar figures have the same shape, but they can have different sizes. Matching angles must be equal, and matching sides must grow or shrink by the same factor.
steps: Match the corresponding angles and check that they are equal.
Match the corresponding sides in the same order.

notes.title: Area ratios of similar figures
notes.explanation: For similar figures, compare corresponding lengths and square their ratio to get the ratio of their areas. If the length ratio is ℓ₁:ℓ₂, the area ratio is ℓ₁²:ℓ₂².
notes.simple: Similar figures keep the same shape. To compare their areas, square the ratio of their matching lengths.
examples: If corresponding lengths are 3:4, the area ratio is 9:16.
If one figure's corresponding length is 3 times the other's, its area is 3² = 9 times the other's area.
steps: Write the ratio of the corresponding lengths.
Square both parts of the ratio.
Write the result as the ratio of the areas.

notes.title: Volume ratios of similar solids
notes.answer: The ratio of the volumes of two similar solids is the cube of the ratio of their corresponding lengths.
notes.explanation: For similar solids, compare corresponding lengths first. Square the length ratio to compare areas, and cube it to compare volumes or masses.
notes.simple: Similar solids have the same shape, even if one is bigger. Their volumes change by the cube of the length scale factor.
examples: If corresponding lengths are 3 and 4, the volume ratio is (3/4)³ = 27/64.
If corresponding lengths are 3 and 2, the surface-area ratio is (3/2)² = 9/4.
steps: Write the ratio of corresponding lengths in the same order as the solids.
For areas, square the length ratio.
